title: 我盘了一圈才想明白:DeFi 出事,多数时候不是没规则,是规则根本不算数
subTitle:
过去两年踩的坑,让我养成一个习惯:每次一个协议爆雷,我不先看"亏了多少",我先看"它本来有没有规则、为什么没拦住"。盘到最后得出一个有点反直觉的结论——绝大多数出事的金库和借贷池,账面上其实都是有风控的。杠杆上限写了,预言机喂价源写了,准入白名单也列了。
真正的问题是:这些规则几乎都活在链下。一份风控文档、一个多签群里的口头共识、一段跑在服务器上的运营脚本。等行情真正异动的那几分钟,没有任何一层东西会在交易结算之前把它自动拦下来。规则在,但它不强制执行;事后你能翻出聊天记录证明"我们本来是有规定的",可钱已经走了。#ETH 
我把这个叫"规则算不算数"的问题。它有两层:一是能不能强制,二是能不能被验证。
先说强制。链上的尴尬在于,合约只认签名,不认意图。你签了,它就执行,中间没有"批准"这个动作。这也是我去看 Newton Mainnet Beta 时觉得它切口找得准的地方——它没去做又一个风控仪表盘,而是把"审批"本身做成链上的一道工序:每笔交易在落地前先过一条 policy,通过或拒绝,规则第一次有了"能拦住"的能力,而不只是"写在那里"。
再说验证,这点我觉得更被低估。事后监控工具能告诉你发生了什么,但你只能选择相信出这份报告的团队。Newton 的做法是每次检查都返回一个签名的 pass/fail 凭证记到链上,配合 Succinct 这类 ZK 方案,让"我确实在结算前按规则检查过"这件事本身变得可证明,而不是"你信我就行"。对真要把几十亿放进去的资金方来说,这个差别不小:它把风控从"信任某个团队"挪到了"链上可强制 + 可验证"。
那规则由谁来定?这是我一开始最担心的——一个项目自己拍脑袋写的 policy,凭什么比金库团队自己的强。Newton 的解法是把机构级的判断直接编进去:合规和安全这块拉了 Chainalysis、Hexagate,金库数据有 Vaults.fyi,风险与评级有 RedStone、Credora,底层安全还叠了 Eigen Labs、Octane 这些。换句话说,它不想自己当那个"风控权威",而是想做承载这些权威规则的那层地基。#BTC 
它从金库切入是务实的:现在 curated vault 里躺着的资金在快速变大,而风控偏偏是最散、最链下的一环,痛点最实。但官方画的更大的图是 Internet of Policies——一个策略的市场,金库只是第一站,后面是 RWA、稳定币,最终到 AI agent。逻辑是自洽的:只要一类资产开始追求"规模化 + 受监管 + 可自动执行",它就需要一层"钱动之前的审批",而这层最好是中立的、可复用的。
$NEWT 是驱动这套授权网络运转的代币——谁来跑 policy、凭什么被信任、作恶如何被惩罚,都绕不开它。23 号会公布启动伙伴,我比较想看的不是又有哪些大牌站台,而是到底谁愿意第一个把自己金库的规则,真的交给这层去强制执行——那才是这套叙事从 PPT 落到链上的第一个实证。
我的判断:DeFi 这一轮要往机构和真实资金走,卡点早就不是收益率,而是"规则算不算数"。监控解决不了这个问题,因为它永远慢一步。把审批搬到结算之前、再让它可验证,听起来不性感,却可能是这类资金敢不敢进场的那道门槛。谁守住这道门槛,谁就站在了所有资金流动的必经路口。
#Newt  $NEWT @NewtonProtocol

translatedData.title: I thought it through after looking around: in most cases when DeFi goes wrong, it’s not that there are no rules—it’s that the rules don’t really count
translatedData.subTitle:
The pitfalls I encountered over the past two years have made me develop a habit: whenever a protocol blows up, I don’t first look at “how much was lost.” I first ask whether “it ever had rules in the first place, and why weren’t they enforced.” When you trace it all the way through, you arrive at a slightly counterintuitive conclusion—most of the vaults and lending pools that had issues actually had risk controls on paper. The leverage limit was written down, the oracle price feed source was specified, and the allowlist for access was also listed.
The real problem is: these rules mostly live off-chain. A risk-control document, a verbal consensus in a multi-sig group, an operations script running on a server. When the market actually moves unexpectedly—those few minutes—none of those layers will automatically stop it before trade settlement. The rules exist, but they aren’t enforced. Later you can dig up chat logs to prove, “We originally had regulations,” but the money has already moved.#ETH

#BTC #ETH 
When every little fluctuation in growth affects your mood, it means your position size is too large. This isn’t investing—it’s gambling. You’re betting on big or small, on whether prices will rise or fall.

Investing should be viewed from a third-person perspective: regulate your actions, standardize your execution. Draw lines, set take-profit and stop-loss—rather than letting yourself get pulled into the candlestick chart and let the red-and-green moves drive your emotional swings.

Buying the dip to add on a decline, chasing gains when prices rise—saying they’re wrong isn’t the point. Everyone’s trading style differs; everyone needs their own set of trading methods. But any trading method should include take-profit and stop-loss levels.

Without a take-profit: when the price pulls back after rising, you’ll regret why you didn’t leave earlier, why you didn’t close the position. That can lead you to add more, thinking that if you can get back to that level, you’ll make even more.

Without a stop-loss: when the price falls, you’ll keep buying, buying, buying to add and average down, raising your cost. You always feel it will reverse and rebound.

The trading market is a world of rules—everything is built on rules. At the same time, it’s also a magnifying glass that magnifies your flaws and shortcomings in human nature.

Many people think trading is a kind of torment, but I feel it’s more like a process of honing oneself—constantly refining your human nature so you can better examine yourself and change.

Let’s encourage each other.

​Just under a year ago, back in August 2025, ETH was riding an absolute wave of euphoria, hitting a peak of nearly $5,000. Fast forward to mid-2026, and the reality check has been savage. Ethereum is currently scraping the bottom of a brutal slide, hovering right around $1,570. That is a massive 68% drop from its all-time high—making Bitcoin’s recent 53% pullback look like a minor speed bump. 

​The internet is currently full of the usual obituaries claiming Solana has finally killed Ethereum, or that the "World Computer" was a failed experiment. But if you actually pull back the layers, Ethereum’s current pain isn’t coming from a failure of the tech. It’s coming from a strange, painful identity crisis.

​The Two Reasons ETH is Getting Punished

​Ethereum isn't just falling because the crypto market is down; it’s actively underperforming Bitcoin. The ETH/BTC trading ratio has collapsed to multi-year lows. There are two major reasons for this lopsided beating: 

​The Tech Stock Curse: Wall Street doesn't view Ethereum the same way it views Bitcoin. To institutional investors, Bitcoin is "digital gold"—a clunky, simple macro hedge. Ethereum, however, is priced like a hyper-growth tech stock. Because ETH has a massive 0.78 correlation to the Nasdaq 100 index, whenever geopolitical friction or rising interest rates cause tech stocks to bleed, institutional funds dump Ethereum first and fastest.

​The ETF Cold Shoulder: While BlackRock and Fidelity’s Bitcoin ETFs have been massive cash magnets, the spot Ethereum ETFs have suffered the exact opposite fate. ETH vehicles just endured a brutal multi-week streak of consecutive net outflows, bleeding over $700 million. Wall Street simply hasn't figured out how to pitch the "smart contract ecosystem" narrative to traditional retirement accounts yet.

​The Counter-Intuitive Twist: Whales are Quietly Buying

​Here is where the story gets distinctly human, and where the chart watchers are getting confused.

​If you look at raw network activity, things look ghost-town quiet. Active wallet addresses on Ethereum have plummeted by nearly 46% since the start of the year. Retail users have temporarily walked away, exhausted by the choppy market.

​Yet, under the cover of this quietness, on-chain data shows a massive anomaly: the number of "whale" wallets holding between 1,000 and 10,000 ETH spiked to record highs at the exact end of June. Hundreds of thousands of ETH have been pulled off exchanges into private custody over the last few weeks.

​While everyday traders are panic-selling the dip, large funds and corporate treasuries are treating $1,500 as an accumulation fire sale. They are betting heavily on the next major structural milestone: the upcoming "Glamsterdam" upgrade slated for later this year, which is designed to scale Ethereum to 10,000 transactions per second and slash base layer fees by nearly 78%. 

​The Verdict: A Maturity Test, Not a Death Sentence

​Ethereum is currently trapped in the ultimate awkward phase. It’s too large and institutionalized to behave like a wild, explosive altcoin anymore, but it’s still too tied to the tech sector to enjoy Bitcoin’s "safe haven" narrative.

​If buyers can successfully defend the psychological floor at $1,500, the market has a solid foundation for a recovery back toward $1,700 as the Glamsterdam upgrade approaches. If $1,500 snaps, expect a messy, emotional flush down to $1,400 before the dust settles.

​The current scenario isn’t the end of Ethereum. It’s just the painful cost of transition. It is the boring, grinding phase of a decentralized network evolving into boring, global financial infrastructure.

title: Tom Lee Reassures Investors: Ethereum’s Price Drop Is Not the Start of a Bear Market
subTitle:
Ethereum continues to face a difficult period. The second-largest cryptocurrency has fallen another 7% over the past week and is now down nearly 22% over the last month, trading around $1,587. However, Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee believes the recent decline has little to do with Ethereum’s underlying fundamentals and is instead driven by temporary institutional trading activity.
He also emphasized that Bitmine has continued accumulating ETH despite the sell-off and is getting closer to owning 5% of Ethereum’s total circulating supply.

Quarter-End Selling Is Driving the Decline, Says Tom Lee
According to Tom Lee, the recent weakness is largely the result of "window dressing," a common quarter-end strategy in which institutional fund managers reduce exposure to underperforming assets before reporting portfolio holdings.
Lee explained that these portfolio adjustments are routine across financial markets and should not be interpreted as a sign of weakening long-term fundamentals for Ethereum.
Over the past month, Ethereum has declined by roughly 22%, compared with Bitcoin’s approximately 19% loss during the same period. Despite the recent underperformance, Lee remains optimistic about Ethereum’s long-term prospects.
He believes that the continued growth of real-world asset tokenization, broader blockchain adoption on Wall Street, and the expansion of AI-powered payment systems will continue to strengthen Ethereum’s position in the years ahead.

Bitmine Continues Aggressively Buying Ethereum
While Ethereum’s price continues to decline, Bitmine has shown no intention of slowing its accumulation strategy.
During the past week, the company purchased an additional 27,084 ETH, increasing its total holdings to approximately 5,700,040 ETH. At current market prices, those holdings are valued at nearly $9 billion.
Bitmine now controls roughly 4.7% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, leaving the company just 0.3 percentage points away from its long-term objective of owning 5% of all ETH.
Lee stressed that Ethereum’s current market price does not accurately reflect the network’s improving fundamentals.
"We're in a period where price is lagging fundamentals."
He added that Ethereum continues to strengthen its role as the leading infrastructure for real-world asset tokenization, institutional blockchain adoption, and future AI-driven financial applications.

Whale Selling Continues to Pressure ETH
Short-term selling pressure has also intensified due to activity from large investors.
Crypto analyst Ali Martinez reported that Ethereum whales sold nearly 550,000 ETH over the past week, worth approximately $880 million at current prices.
The heavy selling pushed Ethereum below the key $1,633 support level.
According to Martinez's technical analysis, Ethereum is now testing support around $1,583. If buyers fail to defend that level, the next major demand zones could be near $1,237 and $1,089.

Open interest is falling, funding rates are compressing, and the US dollar just hit a 40-year high against the yen. That combination tells you more about the next 72 hours of price action than any single headline ever will. Let's break down what the derivatives and funding markets are actually signaling across $BTC and $ETH right now, and why the infrastructure side of crypto could not care less.

Bitcoin is trading at $58,756.44 on Binance, down 2.55% over the past 24 hours with $1.13 billion in daily volume, according to CoinMarketCap. The market cap sits at $1.176 trillion. Ethereum mirrors the weakness at $1,576.49, also down 2.56% on $362.36 million in volume, carrying a market cap of roughly $189.87 billion. Both assets are trading inside well-defined 72-hour ranges, and those ranges matter more than the percentage drops themselves.

Here is the map for $BTC: the 72-hour support sits at $58,201 and resistance caps it at $60,780.57. If bitcoin holds above that $58,201 floor, buyers are effectively defending the bottom of the range and the structure stays intact — that is the dip-buy zone where spot demand has historically stepped in during similar compressions. If it loses $58,201 on volume, the next liquidity pocket gets tested and momentum tilts to sellers. On the upside, a clean break and reclaim above $60,780.57 would signal that the funding reset is complete and directional conviction is returning. For $ETH, the 72-hour support is $1,548.37 with resistance at $1,637.58. Now, what is the derivatives data actually saying beneath these price levels? When funding rates compress alongside falling open interest, it means leveraged longs are being flushed out and the market is de-risking. That is not inherently bearish — it is a reset. The critical question is whether spot demand absorbs the selling or whether the flush cascades. The US dollar strength against the yen, flagged by multiple outlets as a 40-year high, adds a macro headwind. Dollar-denominated assets like crypto face real selling pressure when the greenback surges because global capital rotates into USD instruments. Smart money is positioning for the next leg while the broader market digests macro uncertainty.

【链上有个信号，可能比K线更准】

昨晚凌晨三点，交易所突然流入了将近两万枚ETH。

说白了，大户在动。

价格现在1590附近晃悠，小跌了2%多，七天算下来跌了5%左右。说真的不算意外，但链上数据比K线走得更快——你看到的价格，可能是滞后的。

盖拉蒂给你们拆三个信号：

第一个，方向选择快到了。现在ETH在1520到1650这个区间里磨了挺久，成交量倒是挺活跃，说明资金还在里面折腾，还没彻底躺平。往上还是往下，就看谁先认输。

第二个，情绪其实没有价格跌得那么惨。恐惧指数15，极度恐慌，但你们注意到没，周均才14，基本差不多。这种恐慌更多是情绪传染，不是真出什么大事了。

第三个，也是我最近盯得最紧的——估值。ETH离最高点跌了差不多68%，现在算是超跌区间。问题来了：ETH的基本面变了吗？我当时也问自己，后来发现链上大户地址悄悄在增加，交易所净流量也在降。这不就说明了什么？有的人在悄悄捡。

当然，我也没把握说这就是底。但链上数据不会骗人，价格可以骗人，大户钱包地址骗不了人。

你们觉得呢？

A. 链上信号靠谱，跟着大户走
B. 再等等，情绪还没到底
C. 估值是伪命题，基本面才是王道

I’m not calling a dead-certain short.

I just lean toward this being a signal that “someone has started slowly collecting,” not necessarily that a reversal will happen immediately.

During the day I was drawing and revising and editing until I wanted to cry. At night, alone at my vanity, watching the market, what I fear most is mistaking “there are long-term buyers” for “it’s going to shoot up right away on the short term.”

So on my side, my attitude toward $ETH  is more cautious—I'm not chasing.

If I really do anything, I’ll only wait until the emotions/price action have smoothed out a bit. I don’t want to force a hard buy at this awkward spot. The market turns faster than a book page—keep some dry powder. $ETH #ETH

1. Lighter Updates the LIT Tokenomics Model
Lighter has announced adjustments to the LIT token buyback, burn, and staking incentive mechanisms. Going forward, tokens repurchased through exchange revenues will no longer be retained; instead, they will be burned to continuously tighten circulating supply. The platform disclosed that since the TGE, it has programmatically repurchased approximately 15.5 million LIT, accounting for about 6.3% of the current circulating supply. Meanwhile, the remaining 250 million ecosystem tokens will be used to support staking rewards. The current initial target annualized yield is 6%, and it will be dynamically adjusted later based on market conditions, protocol performance, and sustainability.

2. Shanghai Procuratorate Discloses a Cross-Border Crypto-to-FX Exchange Case Exceeding RMB 200 Million
Prosecutors from the Jing’an District, Shanghai have brought charges against an illegal cross-border virtual-currency exchange case involving more than RMB 200 million. The main offender and four others have been sentenced, with terms ranging from six years to two years and six months, along with fines. The case shows that the involved institutions packaged their business as a “virtual bank app.” Without obtaining foreign exchange business licenses, they provided domestic clients with cross-border asset transfers and FX exchange services, charging about a 3% service fee. This case sends a signal of continued strict supervision over illegal financial activities involving cryptocurrencies.

3. Details of the Illegal FX Exchange Case Exposed; Crypto Counterparty-Trading Pattern Draws Attention
In addition to the verdict, further operational steps are disclosed. The company advertised externally under the name of a “private bank,” guiding customers through intermediaries. Then, internal staff formed groups to facilitate deals, effectively carrying out illegal foreign-exchange conversions. After regulators detected abnormal activity during routine monitoring, they initiated coordination between law enforcement and prosecution and transferred the matter to public security authorities for handling. The case once again reminds the market that virtual assets remain a regulatory focus in cross-border payments, FX exchange, and fund-transfer scenarios, and compliance boundaries are tightening further.

4. bitFlyer Secures CASP Authorization Under the EU MiCA Framework
Japanese crypto exchange bitFlyer announced that its Luxembourg subsidiary, bitFlyer Europe, has obtained CASP authorization from EU regulatory authorities under MiCA, and the authorization is now officially effective. After completing its transformation from VASP to CASP, the platform can expand its service footprint within the region by leveraging the EU passporting mechanism. As the first Japanese exchange to receive this MiCA certification, bitFlyer’s move also reflects how trading platforms are accelerating their layout of compliant markets in Europe, with license competition heating up further.

【Weekend continues to grind the bottom! BTC may still have one last drop, and the real big opportunity is getting closer!】

The market on the weekend is still quite boring.

BTC has been chopping back and forth within a very narrow range, fluctuating up and down without any clear direction. Generally speaking, the truly major move still needs to wait until Monday after the global financial markets open, when capital becomes active again—then the market is more likely to choose a direction.

From the short-term cycle perspective, the 1-hour timeframe remains bearish. MACD is hovering near the zero axis under pressure and has started to turn downward; a dead cross is about to form. This kind of setup is more likely to lead to a second pullback, so everyone should be mentally prepared.

If we see a second test, we will still focus on the prior low around 58,000. Ideally, we can see a downward wick into the $57,800 area to fully flush out the panic sentiment, and then kick off the rebound—this would actually make the foundation for the subsequent rise more solid.

However, when we zoom out to a larger cycle, our view hasn’t changed at all.

BTC has fallen from $126,199 all the way to around $58,000, with a cumulative drop of over 54%. It has now entered the double-top zone from the previous bull cycle, and it’s also the core value range of $54,000–$60,000 that we’ve been emphasizing.

Therefore, for spot positions, we still stick to yesterday’s strategy.

The community has already completed 40% of the mainstream spot allocation (BTC, ETH, SOL). Altcoin allocation is at 10%, with a focus on quality protocol projects such as UNI, AAVE, and HYPE.

For the remaining 60% of funds, we will continue to wait patiently. If the market continues to pull back toward the $54,000 area, we will keep adding in batches according to the plan—not blindly chasing the rally.

The bottom is always ground out through consolidation; it’s not made by one day of dumping. What needs to be done now isn’t guessing the absolute lowest point, but selecting targets in advance, planning your position sizing, and completing the setup during the final wave of panic.

title: Proactive Security: How Newton Mainnet Beta Rewrites Web3 Infrastructure
subTitle:
The current #Web3 security model is broken because it is entirely reactive. Protocols rely on smart contract audits and post-exploit triage, scrambling to save funds after an attack has already occurred. The launch of the Newton Mainnet Beta completely changes this paradigm by introducing a decentralized pre-transaction authorization layer. Instead of reacting to losses, @NewtonProtocol intercepts and evaluates transaction logic against rigid, programmable policies before final settlement happens onchain.
​VaultKit & AI Agent Safety
​At the center of this milestone is VaultKit, an infrastructure engine enabling "compliance-as-code." Developers can now embed immutable boundary rules directly onchain alongside their capital. You can easily configure strict sandboxes for assets—enforcing real-time parameters like maximum daily slippage thresholds, strict allocation caps, or automated destination circuit breakers.
​This infrastructure is also uniquely built to protect the future of automated DeFi. As autonomous AI agents manage more onchain capital, the risk of code bugs or adversarial inputs causing token drains rises. By combining hardware-level Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) with Zero-Knowledge Proofs, Newton guarantees that automated models execute precisely within their authorized boundaries.
​Backed by Economic Security
​Newton’s architecture does not exist in a vacuum. It operates as an EigenLayer Actively Validated Service (AVS), inheriting the massive shared economic security of restaked #ETH $Furthermore, by integrating with robust networks like RedStone Oracles, Newton ensures its pre-transaction checks are fueled by manipulation-resistant data, shielding users from flash-loan vectors.
​Every automated policy check and pre-transaction validation requires computational verification, making the utility of $NEWT central to this ecosystem. The Newton Mainnet Beta isn't just a patch; it’s a necessary primitive for secure, institutional-grade automated execution.
​#Newt

The report is 927 pages long, nearly four times the length of the previous year’s filing (234 pages).

OGE discloses the cover page of the filing, showing that Trump’s 2025 annual financial submission has been completed and signed.

In this report, the largest and most closely watched source of income comes from cryptocurrency.

Last year, Trump earned nearly $1.2 billion from his cryptocurrency businesses. The Associated Press noted that at the time of Trump’s inauguration, these companies were still in their early stages, whereas this year their revenue has already surpassed most of the real estate business he has run for decades. Funding injections from two billionaire investors, along with Trump’s decision to halt the federal crackdown on regulatory pressure aimed at the crypto industry, together helped drive the expansion of these businesses.

More than half of the income comes from his “World Liberty Financial” business. The filing shows that the sales under this operation include new crypto products, including “governance tokens,” with revenue exceeding $500 million. Another crypto business, CIC Digital LLC, contributes even more. The company sells commemorative “meme coins” bearing Trump’s face, generating more than $600 million in revenue. However, because both the governance tokens and the meme coins have fallen sharply since their launch, the value of the related assets has been significantly reduced.

The Associated Press also noted that, in the same period, Trump’s family’s traditional businesses were growing rapidly as well, with the most pronounced expansion coming from its cryptocurrency operations. Last year, the business secured licensing and trading deals in multiple countries, marking its largest overseas expansion to date; among these countries, many are currently negotiating with the United States on matters such as tariffs and military aid.

In addition to cryptocurrency, Trump’s stock holdings are also substantial. The report shows that he holds shares in Apple (AAPL) and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) valued between $5 million and $25 million, as well as holdings in Macy’s (M) and Palantir Technologies (PLTR) valued between $1 million and $5 million. It’s better to wait for the trend to be confirmed and earn a little less than to stubbornly hold against the trend and get trapped. The real opportunity is never something you guess—it’s something you wait for.

title: Altcoins at Historic Lows? Analysts Say 84% of the Market Is Deeply Undervalued
subTitle:
The altcoin market is going through one of its toughest periods in years. According to a new analysis from CryptoQuant, the vast majority of alternative cryptocurrencies are trading well below their long-term price averages, a situation that some analysts describe as unprecedented undervaluation. Others, however, argue that similar conditions have historically marked the beginning of major market recoveries.
The key question now is whether the altcoin era is truly coming to an end—or whether the market is approaching the early stages of its next major rally.

The Vast Majority of Altcoins Continue to Underperform
CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reported that approximately 84% of altcoins are currently trading below their 200-day moving average (200 DMA).
According to him, this reflects the market's prolonged weakness. Every attempt at a meaningful recovery over the past several months has failed, while the total market capitalization of altcoins, excluding Ethereum, continues to decline.
The situation is further confirmed by the weekly close below the 200-day moving average, a signal widely viewed by technical analysts as bearish.
This is far from a short-term correction. Altcoins have now experienced roughly eight consecutive months of underperformance, marking the second-longest period of sustained weakness since 2020.
Darkfost described the current environment as an extended period of stagnation that is severely testing investors' patience.

Could This Sell-Off Be a Buying Opportunity?
Despite the bearish outlook, Darkfost noted that similar market conditions have historically created attractive opportunities for medium-term investors.
This time, however, he believes simply buying the entire market will not be enough. Success will likely depend on carefully selecting projects with strong fundamentals, as not every altcoin is expected to recover equally.
Meanwhile, the total cryptocurrency market capitalization has fallen by approximately 51% from its all-time high and now stands near $2.15 trillion.
Large-cap projects such as BNB, XRP, and Solana remain roughly 60% to 75% below their record highs, while many smaller altcoins continue trading 80% to 90% below their all-time peaks.
Despite these steep declines, the three leading altcoin market indices currently register between 48 and 51 out of 100, indicating neutral sentiment rather than complete market capitulation.

Optimistic Analysts See Early Signs of Recovery
Not everyone shares the bearish outlook.
Market commentator Sykodelic believes current technical conditions are becoming increasingly constructive.
While acknowledging that investor confidence has been severely damaged after several years of disappointing performance, he argues that the first meaningful signs of a recovery are beginning to emerge.
Technical analysts point to the weekly MACD indicator, which has turned positive for the first time in more than two years. They also note that price action appears to be forming a strong bottoming pattern similar to the one that preceded the powerful crypto rally in 2020.

Bitcoin and Ethereum Continue Searching for Direction
The two largest cryptocurrencies have yet to establish a clear recovery trend.
Bitcoin briefly reclaimed the $60,000 level but failed to hold above it and is once again trading below this important psychological threshold.
Ethereum experienced a similar move. Following Bitmine's latest ETH purchase, the cryptocurrency briefly climbed back above $1,600, only to surrender most of those gains and return to around $1,590.

【套了整整一周，我终于想明白了一件事】

打开账户，又是一片绿。说真的，这周我都没勇气天天看行情了。

手里攥着的ETH，就这么眼睁睁看着它从高位跌下来。上周还在想"差不多了吧，应该能反弹"，结果呢？一周下来又跌了6个点，现在1567美元。我都想问自己：你是不是跟钱有仇？

1）The Open USD Stablecoin Alliance has made its debut, with organizations including Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Coinbase, and BlackRock participating. It focuses on returning more of reserve earnings to partner parties; this stablecoin competition is shifting from “who issues” to “who controls distribution and the structure of returns.”
2）The SEC has publicly solicited comments on “new types of ETFs,” covering everything from innovative asset classes to funds with new strategies. For crypto ETFs, prediction-market related products, and single-asset strategy products, the next phase looks more like a repricing of the regulatory framework than simply a matter of approval speed.
3）In Q2, the number of crypto security incidents rose to a high level. Bridges and authorization/management permissions remain the main risk points; when liquidity is weak, the market tends to punish complex DeFi structures and cross-chain exposures more quickly.

Conclusion: Today’s main thread isn’t a single positive or negative catalyst—it’s that stablecoins, ETFs, and on-chain security are all entering a phase of “rules and risk repricing.” In the short term, it’s better to manage position size and wait for confirmation than to chase high-priced narratives.

title: Altcoin Whales Rotate While BTC Hovers Near Critical Support
subTitle:
Liquidity is the tide, and right now the tide is receding from the majors. Bitcoin sits at $58,502 on Binance, down 2.22% over the past 24 hours, while Ethereum trades at $1,571.85, off 1.69%. But scan the broader board and a different picture emerges: M is up 22.3%, H has surged 18.7%, and SYN has rallied 13.5% in the same window, per CoinMarketCap. That divergence tells you exactly where speculative capital is flowing — away from the two largest assets and into mid-cap names with thinner order books and sharper moves. This is textbook altcoin rotation, and understanding the macro plumbing behind it matters more than chasing the green candles.

Start with the dollar. The macro backdrop has shifted into a cautious wait-and-see mode as markets parse whether the Federal Reserve's pause on rate cuts extends deeper into the second half of the year. When dollar liquidity tightens — or even just stalls — the first assets to feel the squeeze are the largest, most institutionally held ones. That is $BTC and $ETH. Hedge funds and ETF allocators reduce risk at the top of the stack first. Meanwhile, retail and smaller crypto-native traders, who tend to play the leverage game in lower-cap names, keep rotating within the ecosystem. The result is the exact spread we see today: red on the benchmarks, green further down the market-cap ladder.

The ETH-specific picture is especially telling. CoinMarketCap data shows Ethereum ETF outflows hit $345 million recently, and with $ETH trading 1.69% lower on the day, those redemption flows are not abstract — they are mechanically selling into spot. The headline asking whether sub-$1,500 is next is not fear-mongering; it is asking a legitimate structural question about whether ETF holders will continue to unwind. On the Binance chart, ETH's 72-hour support sits at $1,548.37, with resistance capping at $1,637.58. If Ethereum holds that $1,548 floor, buyers have a defensible line to build a range — the kind of consolidation that precedes the next directional move. If it loses $1,548 on a closing basis, the next liquidity pocket below becomes the focus, and the ETF outflow narrative accelerates. That is the level to watch — tap $ETH to trade it.

$BTC, meanwhile, is caught in its own narrow corridor. Bitcoin's 72-hour support is $58,201, and resistance is $60,780.57. At $58,502, BTC is barely $300 above its support — essentially pressing its face against the glass. If buyers defend $58,201 and volume picks up, the range holds and the market gets a signal that institutional demand still has a bid. If Bitcoin loses $58,201, the bearish headline about a "$5K best investment opportunity" starts to look less like contrarian wisdom and more like a roadmap. The proximity matters: tight supports that break tend to produce fast moves because stop-losses cluster just below. That is the setup on $BTC right now — tap to open the pair and watch the level in real time.

Now zoom into why the altcoin pumps deserve skepticism rather than FOMO. M, H, and SYN all moved double digits on volumes that pale next to BTC's $1.17 billion daily turnover. These rotations are liquidity-seeking trades — capital sloshing into the most volatile venue it can find when the big caps go quiet. That works until it does not. When BTC and ETH break decisively in one direction, the altcoin bids evaporate almost instantly because the same traders are the marginal buyers across the board. The headline about Strategy's capital overhaul easing "death spiral" fears is relevant here: confidence in the largest holders matters because if they dump, the ripples hit the small caps hardest.

The regime read is straightforward. We are in a risk-off drift at the top of the crypto stack, with speculative excess bubbling in the lower tiers. That pattern holds until macro liquidity — whether from Fed policy, dollar weakness, or a fresh catalyst — re-enters the system and lifts the entire complex. Until then, the map is clear: $BTC needs to hold $58,201 and reclaim $60,780 to signal buyers are back in control; $ETH needs to hold $1,548 and push toward $1,637 to slow the ETF bleed. Anything else is noise.

Not financial advice.

1、Event Overview

Today’s on-chain monitoring shows that FG Nexus has transferred the final 9,481 ETH to Galaxy Digital, meaning all of the ETH it previously held has been fully liquidated. Based on the disclosed data, the address has cumulatively deposited approximately 51,156 ETH, worth about $109.4 million in total, with final cumulative losses of roughly $86.6 million. For the market, this is not an ordinary de-risking move, but rather a fairly thorough risk-clearance signal. Especially while ETH prices remain in a price-sensitive range where positioning and capital competition are active, a large address’s “liquidation-style transfer” is often interpreted by the market as either a near-term bearish signal or a strategy prioritizing liquidity.📉

2、Background and Behavioral Analysis

In terms of the execution path, FG Nexus did not choose a dispersed on-chain sell-off. Instead, it continuously moved assets to institutional channels such as Galaxy Digital. This usually suggests a preference to complete the disposal through OTC execution, market making, or other institutional settlement methods, so as to reduce market impact on public order books. Such behavior typically appears in two scenarios: (1) passive stop-loss actions or rising pressure to retrieve funds, and (2) proactively ending the asset-allocation logic of a particular cycle.

It’s worth noting that the massive loss itself is even more important to analyze than the act of “selling.” A $86.6 million loss indicates its entry cost was significantly higher than the current realized level, and it also reflects that even large capital can’t avoid timing mistakes in a high-volatility market. What the market is paying closer attention to recently is not just how much FG Nexus sold, but whether institutions or whales like this are shifting from “continue holding and waiting for a recovery” toward a defensive pattern of “take profits first, then observe.” If similar addresses continue to show synchronized de-risking afterward, it may reinforce the market’s cautious expectations for risk appetite in the short to mid term.🤔

3、Market Impact and Follow-Up Monitoring

In the short run, FG Nexus completing the full liquidation may actually help release some sell-pressure and make it easier for the market to digest. In other words, the market’s biggest worry—“potential supply not yet sold”—has been reduced. If there is no new wave of sell orders of the same magnitude to take its place, ETH’s price may not face continued downward pressure as a direct result. For the medium term, two points matter: first, the flow after Galaxy Digital takes custody—whether it is further distributed to trading platforms or moved into longer-term institutional arrangements; second, whether on-chain activity shows more large ETH being transferred and concentrated toward market makers, custodians, or exchanges.

Overall, the key message conveyed by this news is not that a single address is simply exiting at a loss, but that the current ETH market is still in a phase of sentiment adjustment and capital rebalancing. For investors, it’s more important to watch the flow of large on-chain funds, changes in net inflows into institutional channels, and the market’s capacity to absorb demand—not to make emotional judgments based only on a single event like a “whale liquidation.” The large losses suffered by professional capital again underline that in volatile markets, position management and liquidity arrangements are often more important than directional calls.⚠️

1、事件概述

今日链上监测显示，FG Nexus已将最后9481枚ETH转入Galaxy Digital，意味着其此前持有的ETH已完成全部清仓。按披露数据计算，该地址累计转入约5.1156万枚ETH，总价值约1.094亿美元，最终累计亏损约8660万美元。对市场而言，这不是一笔普通减仓，而是一次较为彻底的风险出清信号。尤其在当前ETH价格仍处于资金博弈敏感区间时，大额地址的“清仓式转移”容易被市场解读为阶段性看空或流动性优先策略。📉

2、背景与行为分析

从操作路径看，FG Nexus并未选择分散式链上抛售，而是持续向Galaxy Digital这类机构通道转移资产，这通常意味着其更倾向于通过场外、做市或机构执行方式完成处置，以降低公开市场冲击。这类行为往往出现在两种情境中：一是被动止损或资金回笼压力上升，二是主动结束某一周期内的资产配置逻辑。

值得注意的是，巨额亏损本身比“卖出”更值得分析。8660万美元的损失说明其建仓成本显著高于当前兑现水平，也反映出在高波动市场中，即使是大资金也难以避免择时失误。最近市场更关注的不只是FG Nexus卖了多少，而是这类机构或巨鲸是否正在从“继续持有等待修复”转向“先落袋、再观察”的防守模式。若类似地址后续继续出现同步减仓，可能强化市场对中短期风险偏好的谨慎预期。🤔

3、市场影响与后续观察

短线来看，FG Nexus完成清仓反而可能释放一部分抛压落地信号。也就是说，市场最担心的“未卖出的潜在筹码”已经减少，若后续没有新的同等级抛售接力，ETH价格未必因此持续承压。中期则要看两点：第一，Galaxy Digital接手后的流向，是进一步分发至交易平台，还是进入更长期的机构安排；第二，链上是否出现更多大额ETH向做市商、托管机构或交易所集中转移。

整体来看，这则消息传递出的核心不是单一地址亏损离场，而是当前ETH市场仍处于情绪与资金再平衡阶段。对投资者而言，更应关注链上大额资金流向、机构通道净流入变化以及市场承接能力，而不是仅凭单笔“巨鲸清仓”作出情绪化判断。专业资金的大幅亏损再次说明，波动市场中仓位管理和流动性安排，往往比方向判断更重要。⚠️

title: White House Targets July 4 for CLARITY Act: Will Crypto's Biggest Bill Make the Deadline?
subTitle:
By Emtiaz a Binancian 
---
Introduction
The most trending topic of Binance Square today, what? I guess you've seen it everywhere — #w#WhiteHouseTargetsJuly4ForClarityActPassage has amassed over 311,000 views and nearly 1,900 discussions. And for good reason. This could be the most consequential piece of crypto legislation in U.S. history — and the clock is ticking.
Today is July 1. The White House wants the CLARITY Act passed by July 4. But with the Senate adjourned until July 13 and a mountain of unresolved issues still on the table, the question isn't just will it pass — it's can it pass?
Let's break down what's really happening.
---
What Is the CLARITY Act?
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act is Washington's long-overdue attempt to answer the most basic question in crypto regulation: who's in charge of what?
For years, the industry has operated in a regulatory gray zone — uncertain whether tokens fall under the SEC (securities) or the CFTC (commodities). The CLARITY Act draws a clear line:
Most cryptocurrencies would be classified as digital commodities under CFTC oversight
· Investment contracts tied to digital assets would remain under SEC jurisdiction
· Stablecoins would fall under joint oversight
The bill also extends Bank Secrecy Act requirements to crypto brokers, dealers, and exchanges — mandating anti-money laundering programs, customer identification, and sanctions compliance.
Supporters say this framework would end years of uncertainty, making it easier for banks, asset managers, and institutions to launch tokenized products and custody services.
---
The Timeline: What's Happened So Far
· July 2025: House passed its version (H.R. 3633) in a 294-134 bipartisan vote
· May 14, 2026: Senate Banking Committee advanced its version 15-9
· May 2026: Patrick Witt announced the White House's July 4 target at Consensus Miami
· June 13, 2026: Witt reaffirmed the July 4 goal in a live interview
· Today (July 1): The Senate remains adjourned until July 13
---
The Bull Case: Why It Could Still Happen
Patrick Witt, Executive Director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets, remains optimistic. He says discussions are advancing daily across three priority areas flagged by Democratic senators: agriculture-related jurisdiction, ethics, and developer protections ("BRCA").
"We're making progress on all fronts, every day. Groups are at the table, trading paper. So, I'm still optimistic that we could hit that timeline." — Patrick Witt
Senator Tim Scott struck an even more confident tone, saying on Fox Business that the CLARITY Act "will pass" before the August recess.
Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz spent 10 hours meeting with 14 senators and said the bill is down to three solvable issues — including ethics.
Senator Cynthia Lummis has also said the Senate is preparing to move forward with the legislation in July. She previously warned that failure to pass before the August recess could push the next viable window all the way to 2030.
---
The Bear Case: Why July 4 Looks "Logistically Impossible"
Journalist Eleanor Terrett has been one of the most vocal skeptics. Her verdict was blunt: passing the CLARITY Act by July 4 is "logistically impossible".
Here's what would need to happen in roughly two weeks:
1. Find ethics language both parties can accept
2. Resolve issues in the Agriculture Committee's text
3. Merge separate Senate bills from Banking and Agriculture committees
4. Secure 60 votes in the Senate
5. Pass it through both chambers
None of this is finished.
The Senate Banking version still must be reconciled with the Agriculture Committee's companion bill — and jurisdiction over the SEC and CFTC is split between them.
The 60-Vote Problem
Republicans hold 53 seats. Even with every Republican voting yes, they'd still need at least 7 Democratic senators to cross over.
But full Republican support isn't guaranteed — Senators Josh Hawley and Rand Paul opposed the GENIUS Act. And Democratic support may depend on stronger ethics provisions addressing President Trump's crypto interests.
Prediction markets reflect the uncertainty:
· Polymarket: 48% chance of 2026 passage (down from 70% in mid-May)
· Galaxy Research: Cut odds from 60% to 50%
· Kalshi: 46% chance of year-end passage
---
What's at Stake for the Market
Jefferies warned that political uncertainty could fuel elevated volatility across crypto markets in the coming weeks.
If the Act Passes ✅
· Institutional floodgates open — banks, asset managers, and exchanges get the regulatory framework they need
· Tokenized securities accelerate — ETF offerings expand beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum
· Crypto infrastructure IPOs could revive
· XRP and other compliant institutional layers could benefit significantly
If It Delays or Fails ❌
· Regulatory uncertainty extends — agency actions can be reversed by future administrations
· Institutions slow blockchain initiatives while reassessing legal risks
· Grayscale warned that stalled legislation could pressure Bitcoin and digital asset treasury firms
· Next viable window may not open until 2030
---
How Smart Money Is Playing This
As one Binance Square user put it:
"Most traders fail on Binance Square because they trade the news of yesterday. If you want to earn like the top 2%, you need to look at where the massive institutional liquidity is rotating right now."
The 98% are waiting for the bill to pass to buy. The 2% are buying the accumulation zones right now — specifically positioning into compliant institutional layers like XRP and Ethereum settlement rails.
Meanwhile, smart capital is also watching the gold vs. Bitcoin rotation — using algorithmic yield-bearing stablecoins to capture spreads while the two asset classes battle for dominance.
---
Final Thoughts
July 4 is just days away. But with the Senate not even in session until July 13, the White House's original deadline appears increasingly difficult to meet.
That doesn't mean the bill is dead. Senate leaders are still pushing for a July vote, and the August recess is the real make-or-break deadline.
But one thing is clear: regulatory clarity is coming — whether this month, this year, or beyond. The question for traders isn't if — it's when.
And more importantly: is your portfolio positioned for what comes next?
Thanks for your time

content:
Woke up to my group chats looking like a boxing ring today. Everyone screaming over this "compliant" protocol. And honestly? I just scrolled past because I've been burned too many times by shiny tech promises.

Let me tell you why this whole @NewtonProtocol thing gives me actual anxiety.

Last month,I saw ETH flash crash to $3,100 for literally three seconds,My heart nearly jumped out of my chest,I smashed that swap button faster than I've ever done anything in my life—no thinking, just pure adrenaline,But my RPC was congested,That half-second delay cost me,I got filled at $3,190 instead.

Still made a little profit, but man... watching that perfect entry slip away while your screen buffers? That sting sticks with you.

Now imagine that delay isn't just random network congestion. It's a mandatory checkpoint. Your transaction has to stop, go through compliance checks, verify you're not a bad guy, and then hit the chain. Meanwhile, the market has already moved two full candles.

That's exactly what Newton is rolling out with their Mainnet Beta. ZK-proofs, TEEs, all that fancy stuff—cool, I get it, regulators love it. But I don't want to relive that helpless feeling of watching my screen freeze while the market eats my limit order.

DeFi's whole beauty was cutting out the middleman and the red tape. This feels like we're building the red tape right back into the code. And retail traders like you and me are gonna be the ones eating terrible slippage when things get volatile.

I'm not saying it's trash, I'm just saying I've learned my lesson, I'm not putting my liquidity anywhere that makes me wait in line while the opportunity passes me by.

If I wanted compliance delays, I'd just go back to using a bank.

Am I overreacting or does this actually scare you too?

title: White House Targets July 4 for CLARITY Act: Will Crypto's Biggest Bill Make the Deadline?
subTitle:
By Emtiaz 
Introductio:
As per concern, I think here I am prrsenting one of the most trending topic of Binance Square today, and I guess you've seen it everywhere — #WhiteHouseTargetsJuly4ForClarityActPassage has amassed over 311,000 views and nearly 1,900 discussions. And for good reason. This could be the most consequential piece of crypto legislation in U.S. history — and the clock is ticking.
Today is July 1. The White House wants the CLARITY Act passed by July 4. But with the Senate adjourned until July 13 and a mountain of unresolved issues still on the table, the question isn't just will it pass — it's can it pass?
Let's break down what's really happening.
---
What Is the CLARITY Act?
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act is Washington's long-overdue attempt to answer the most basic question in crypto regulation: who's in charge of what?
For years, the industry has operated in a regulatory gray zone — uncertain whether tokens fall under the SEC (securities) or the CFTC (commodities). The CLARITY Act draws a clear line:
· Most cryptocurrencies would be classified as digital commodities under CFTC oversight
· Investment contracts tied to digital assets would remain under SEC jurisdiction
· Stablecoins would fall under joint oversight
The bill also extends Bank Secrecy Act requirements to crypto brokers, dealers, and exchanges — mandating anti-money laundering programs, customer identification, and sanctions compliance.
Supporters say this framework would end years of uncertainty, making it easier for banks, asset managers, and institutions to launch tokenized products and custody services.
---
The Timeline: What's Happened So Far
· July 2025: House passed its version (H.R. 3633) in a 294-134 bipartisan vote
· May 14, 2026: Senate Banking Committee advanced its version 15-9
· May 2026: Patrick Witt announced the White House's July 4 target at Consensus Miami
· June 13, 2026: Witt reaffirmed the July 4 goal in a live interview
· Today (July 1): The Senate remains adjourned until July 13
---
The Bull Case: Why It Could Still Happen
Patrick Witt, Executive Director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets, remains optimistic. He says discussions are advancing daily across three priority areas flagged by Democratic senators: agriculture-related jurisdiction, ethics, and developer protections ("BRCA").
"We're making progress on all fronts, every day. Groups are at the table, trading paper. So, I'm still optimistic that we could hit that timeline." — Patrick Witt
Senator Tim Scott struck an even more confident tone, saying on Fox Business that the CLARITY Act "will pass" before the August recess.
Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz spent 10 hours meeting with 14 senators and said the bill is down to three solvable issues — including ethics.
Senator Cynthia Lummis has also said the Senate is preparing to move forward with the legislation in July. She previously warned that failure to pass before the August recess could push the next viable window all the way to 2030.
---
The Bear Case: Why July 4 Looks "Logistically Impossible"
Journalist Eleanor Terrett has been one of the most vocal skeptics. Her verdict was blunt: passing the CLARITY Act by July 4 is "logistically impossible".
Here's what would need to happen in roughly two weeks:
1. Find ethics language both parties can accept
2. Resolve issues in the Agriculture Committee's text
3. Merge separate Senate bills from Banking and Agriculture committees
4. Secure 60 votes in the Senate
5. Pass it through both chambers
None of this is finished.
The Senate Banking version still must be reconciled with the Agriculture Committee's companion bill — and jurisdiction over the SEC and CFTC is split between them.
The 60-Vote Problem
Republicans hold 53 seats. Even with every Republican voting yes, they'd still need at least 7 Democratic senators to cross over.
But full Republican support isn't guaranteed — Senators Josh Hawley and Rand Paul opposed the GENIUS Act. And Democratic support may depend on stronger ethics provisions addressing President Trump's crypto interests.
Prediction markets reflect the uncertainty:
· Polymarket: 48% chance of 2026 passage (down from 70% in mid-May)
· Galaxy Research: Cut odds from 60% to 50%
· Kalshi: 46% chance of year-end passage
---
What's at Stake for the Market
Jefferies warned that political uncertainty could fuel elevated volatility across crypto markets in the coming weeks.
If the Act Passes ✅
· Institutional floodgates open — banks, asset managers, and exchanges get the regulatory framework they need
· Tokenized securities accelerate — ETF offerings expand beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum
· Crypto infrastructure IPOs could revive
· XRP and other compliant institutional layers could benefit significantly
If It Delays or Fails ❌
· Regulatory uncertainty extends — agency actions can be reversed by future administrations
· Institutions slow blockchain initiatives while reassessing legal risks
· Grayscale warned that stalled legislation could pressure Bitcoin and digital asset treasury firms
· Next viable window may not open until 2030
---
How Smart Money Is Playing This
As one Binance Square user put it:
"Most traders fail on Binance Square because they trade the news of yesterday. If you want to earn like the top 2%, you need to look at where the massive institutional liquidity is rotating right now."
The 98% are waiting for the bill to pass to buy. The 2% are buying the accumulation zones right now — specifically positioning into compliant institutional layers like XRP and Ethereum settlement rails.
Meanwhile, smart capital is also watching the gold vs. Bitcoin rotation — using algorithmic yield-bearing stablecoins to capture spreads while the two asset classes battle for dominance.
---
Final Thoughts
July 4 is just days away. But with the Senate not even in session until July 13, the White House's original deadline appears increasingly difficult to meet.
Thanks for your 
This is Emtiaz signing off for now.

The ecosystem is running, staking is running, and Layer 2 solutions are still moving forward. With the price falling this far, how much of it is due to changes in fundamentals, and how much is just the market’s emotional stampede? That’s worth thinking through.

My conclusion: next week, the key is to watch whether support at 1520 can hold. If it breaks, the next level to watch is directly around 1400. But if trading volume continues to expand and the rebound follows through, then resistance at 1642 will be the real test.
